explanations: luna: The section's fall through life's stages and return to judgment meet the sequence of being lifeless, revived, made to die, revived again, then returned to God.
terra: The people are told to enter the town, eat freely from it, and enter the gate humbly for forgiveness; 2:59 shows provisioned place reversed by disobedience.
terra: The wrongdoers change the commanded word and receive punishment from heaven, the adverse turn inside the freely provisioned town of 2:58.
terra: Allah raises the Mount over the covenant people and commands them to hold the Book firmly, joining the mountain place to an enacted demand for durable religious adherence.

luna: The section's الْبَلَدِ الْأَمِينِ meets the sanctuary made a place of return and safety, مَثَابَةً لِّلنَّاسِ وَأَمْنًا; the place is both refuge and center. | terra: The House is made “a place of return and security” (مَثَابَةً … وَأَمْنًا), joining sacred place, coming back, and safety immediately before Abraham’s provision prayer.

luna: The section's secure town joins safety to provision; Abraham asks for a town that is safe, بَلَدًا آمِنًا, and for its people to receive fruits. | terra: Abraham asks that the town be secure and that its believing people be provided fruits, exactly the two qualities the section assigns to the sworn city.
terra: Abraham and Ishmael raise the House’s foundations and ask that their work be accepted; beside 2:125–126, sound construction, acceptance, safe place, and provision form one scene.

luna: The section says رَدّ has the dictionary sense of turning back from religion; this ayah names turning back from dīn and losing one's works, a precise religious reversal. | terra: Whoever “turns back from his religion” (يَرْتَدِدْ … عَن دِينِهِ) and dies faithless has his works rendered void, directly joining the r-d-d family’s apostasy sense to rejected work.
terra: The one who rejects false gods and believes in Allah grasps the firmest handhold, “with no breaking in it,” a concrete unbroken support on the faith side of the section's cut-rope image.
terra: The observer is shown bones being raised and clothed with flesh, a resurrection scene that answers the section’s dictionary image of a bone’s faulty or repaired joining.
terra: Spending is pictured as a grain yielding seven hundred grains, the durable multiplied work whose reward is protected from mann and injury in 2:262.

terra: Those who spend without following it by mann (reminding others of their favor) or injury retain their reward with their Lord; this Quranic sense of مَنّ sits directly beside the section’s “uncut reward.”

terra: The command not to nullify charity through mann and harm, followed by the rain-stripped rock, turns a supposedly good work into one that leaves no yield, matching the rejected or spoiled workmanship in the section.
terra: Sincere spending is a high garden that doubles its crop under rain, the productive counterpart to the rain-stripped barren rock of 2:264.
terra: The usurer rises on Resurrection in a disordered manner after falsely equating usury with trade; commercial value, moral distortion, and bodily standing before judgment meet in one ayah.

luna: The section's root ح ك م includes making something firm; this ayah distinguishes firmly established verses, مُحْكَمَاتٌ, from ambiguous ones, a textual instance of that quality. | terra: The Book contains “firmly established ayat” (ءَايَٰتٌ مُّحْكَمَٰتٌ), the root’s secured-construction side that the section places beside judging.
terra: Allah promises the return of all to Him and then His judgment concerning their differences, a close non-r-d-d parallel to return and divine adjudication.

luna: The section's returned, faulty coin meets a Qur'anic dinar entrusted to one who returns it, while another refuses its return; the ayah makes trust and coin-value meet concretely. | terra: One person entrusted with a treasure returns it, while another entrusted with a dinar does not; the ayah joins the section’s dinar, trust, and return in a commercial test.
terra: Even an earth-full of gold would not be accepted as ransom from one who dies faithless, setting the strongest possible market value against divine rejection.
terra: Abraham’s standing-place is among the House’s signs, and whoever enters it is secure, joining the sacred locale to both qiyām imagery and safety.

luna: The section's dictionary sense of م ن ن includes a cut rope, while this ayah tells believers to hold together to God's rope, حَبْلِ اللَّهِ, and not split apart; it offers a specific image of a bond kept intact. | terra: Believers must hold together to Allah's rope and not divide, the direct communal opposite of the severed rope used to explain interrupted reward.
terra: Believers are told not to weaken or grieve because they will be “the uppermost,” the faith-conditioned reversal of being brought to the lowest.
terra: The warning says obeying the faithless would turn believers back on their heels, so they would return as losers; bodily reversal figures religious reversal.
luna: The section's life ending and reward uncut meet those killed in God's path who are not dead but alive and provided for; death does not stop their life with God.
luna: The section's wage continuing beyond bodily descent meets the rejoicing of those alive with their Lord over His bounty; this neighbor specifies their continuing provision.
luna: The section's enduring wage meets the assurance that God does not waste believers' reward, لَا يُضِيعُ أَجْرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ; this completes the promise in 3:169–170.
terra: Every soul tastes death and receives its wages in full only on Resurrection, joining the end of lifespan to an undiminished final payment.
terra: Allah promises never to waste the work of any worker, male or female, and attaches recompense to costly faithful action, directly preserving both labor and its wage.
terra: Wealth is described as something Allah made qiyām for people and as the source from which they are provided, extending q-w-m from bodily support to economic sustenance.
luna: The section's returned counterfeit and just ruling meet the command to restore trusts and judge among people with justice, بِالْعَدْلِ; both benches depend on a fair standard.
terra: Disputed matters must be “referred back” (فَرُدُّوهُ) to Allah and the Messenger if people believe, using r-d-d as the route to authoritative judgment.
terra: People do not truly believe until they make the Messenger judge their disputes and submit without inner resistance, making judgment a boundary of faith.
luna: The section's wage that survives life's cutoff meets the migrant who dies on the way: his reward has fallen to God's account, فَقَدْ وَقَعَ أَجْرُهُ عَلَى اللَّهِ.
terra: Satan promises to command people to alter Allah’s creation; this is the explicit hostile boundary against 30:30’s unchangeable fitrah and divinely set form.

luna: The section's root ق و م links bodily uprightness with measured justice; this verse commands people to stand persistently for justice even against themselves or kin. | terra: Believers are commanded to stand firmly for justice as witnesses even against themselves and their families, directly joining q-w-m posture to equitable judgment.

luna: The section notes that أَسْفَل also names Hell's lowest depth; this verse places hypocrites in the lowest level, a specific infernal counterpart to the human's fall. | terra: The hypocrites are in “the lowest depth of the Fire” (ٱلدَّرْكِ ٱلْأَسْفَلِ), the Quranic destination that gives the section’s spatial “lowest” reading its severe boundary.

luna: The section's upright human, sound measure, and just judge meet the command to stand firm for God as witnesses in justice, كُونُوا قَوَّامِينَ لِلَّهِ شُهَدَاءَ بِالْقِسْطِ. | terra: Believers are commanded to stand for Allah as witnesses in justice and not let hatred bend them from justice, making upright stance an enacted judicial straightness.
terra: The ayah commands judgment by revelation, urges competition in good works, and ends with everyone’s return to Allah, uniting the section’s judge, sound work, and return.
terra: The question “Who is better than Allah in judgment?” opposes divine judgment to the judgment of ignorance, directly illuminating the closing question of surah 95.

luna: The section's dictionary sense of رَدّ as apostasy meets the question who would turn back from religion; the verse contrasts apostasy with a people God loves and who love Him. | terra: Whoever turns back from religion (يَرْتَدَّ … عَن دِينِهِ) will be replaced by a people Allah loves, another explicit apostasy sense of the section’s r-d-d family.
terra: Game within reach of hands and spears tests who fears Allah unseen; the section’s straight spear appears here as a functioning implement whose use exposes the worker’s obedience.
terra: Allah made the Kaaba “a support/standing for people” (قِيَٰمًا لِّلنَّاسِ), bringing the secure sacred place into the q-w-m family that holds the human form upright.

luna: The section says the fifth verse's رَدّ and the eighth verse's judgment meet; here people are returned to their true master and الحكم is His, فَرُدُّوا إِلَى اللَّهِ مَوْلَاهُمُ الْحَقِّ. | terra: People are “returned to Allah, their true Master” (رُدُّوا۟ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ مَوْلَىٰهُمُ ٱلْحَقِّ), and the same ayah declares that judgment is His, directly joining return and judgment.
terra: Abraham turns his face toward the One who created heaven and earth, upright and free of association, a direct creation-and-directed-religion parallel to 30:30.
terra: People come to Allah alone as He created them the first time, leaving gifts behind while their claimed intercessors and inventions vanish; first creation, return, and failed fabrication meet.
terra: People assign partners and invent sons and daughters for Allah even though He created them; 6:101 answers the fabrication with the Creator's absolute making.
terra: The Originator of heaven and earth has no consort and created everything, supplying real creation as the answer to the invented relations of 6:100.
terra: The speaker refuses to seek any judge besides Allah, who sent the Book fully detailed, placing divine adjudication beside a completed, well-determined text.

luna: The section's full-weight coin and fair judgment meet the command to complete measure and weight in justice, بِالْقِسْطِ; the verse makes honest measure a divine rule. | terra: The command to fulfill measure and balance with justice extends exact assay into covenantal conduct.

luna: The section links upright human form with the root ق و م and dīn; this ayah names Abraham's straight path and a correct religion, دِينًا قِيَمًا. | terra: The Prophet is guided to a straight path and “an upright religion” (دِينًا قِيَمًا), another Quranic use in which q-w-m describes religion rather than a body or tool.

luna: The section's sound work weighed for reward meets the true weighing on that Day, فَمَن ثَقُلَتْ مَوَازِينُهُ; deeds receive an actual measure. | terra: The weighing on that Day is truth, and people with heavy scales prosper; 7:9 supplies the deficient opposite.

luna: The section's sound deed that holds its value is set against the light scale and loss here; this ayah states the contrary outcome of misweighted deeds. | terra: Those whose scales are light lose themselves because they wronged Allah's signs, joining failed weight, denial, and the adverse verdict.

luna: The section's creation and straightening meeting recalls God's creation and forming of humanity before the command to bow; the verse makes the form a setting for moral response. | terra: Allah creates and fashions humanity before commanding the angels to bow to Adam; 7:13 then shows Iblis's proud claim ending in descent and abasement.
terra: Iblis’s proud claim to height is answered, “descend” and be among the abased, showing a moral descent in which self-exaltation produces lowness.
terra: At the descent, earth becomes a temporary settlement and provision; 7:25 then names life, death, and renewed emergence from that ground.
terra: People live and die in earth and will be brought out from it, completing 7:24's descent into a measured earthly stay.

luna: The section's dictionary family for بَلَد includes earth and soil; this ayah sends rain to a dead land and says that is how the dead are brought forth. | terra: Rain is driven to “a dead land” (بَلَدٍ مَّيِّتٍ), brings out fruit, and is explicitly likened to bringing out the dead, joining the balad family’s soil face to resurrection.
terra: Good land brings out growth by its Lord's permission, while bad land yields only meagerly, making the ground itself an image of sound and defective yield.
terra: The chiefs of ʿĀd tell Hūd that they think he is a liar; 7:68 answers that charge with his claim to be a trustworthy adviser.
terra: Hūd calls himself “a trustworthy adviser” directly after his people call him a liar, placing reliability and takdhîb's opposite in one exchange.

luna: The section's sarraf tests a coin's weight and rejects the faulty one; Shuʿayb commands full measure and weight and forbids depriving people, وَزِنُوا بِالْقِسْطَاسِ الْمُسْتَقِيمِ. | terra: Shuʿayb commands his people to give full measure and weight and not diminish people’s goods, a commercial version of sound, unrejected value.
terra: Shuʿayb asks his two opposed communities to wait until Allah judges between them and calls Him the best of judges, giving the closing title a communal dispute scene.

luna: The section's secure town and provision meet the promise that believing, God-fearing towns would receive blessings from heaven and earth, بَرَكَاتٍ مِّنَ السَّمَاءِ وَالْأَرْضِ. | terra: Had the towns believed and been mindful, blessings from heaven and earth would have opened; because they denied, they were seized, joining belief, denial, provision, and reversal.
luna: The section's safe town's reversal meets the question whether people of towns feel secure at night; the ayah makes apparent security the subject of warning.
luna: The section's safety and provision meet the parallel warning about towns struck at forenoon while playing; this neighboring verse completes the reversal begun at 7:97.

terra: When Allah manifests to the mountain it is leveled and Moses falls unconscious, then recovers and glorifies Allah; the Mount scene itself stages height, collapse, restored awareness, and judgment before divine presence.
terra: Those who hold fast to the Book and establish prayer are reformers, and Allah says He does not waste the reward of reformers, joining q-w-m worship, repaired conduct, and preserved pay.
terra: The mountain is raised above the people like a canopy and they are told to hold firmly to revelation, repeating the Mount-and-firmness scene.
terra: The formerly weak and fearful people are sheltered, supported, and provided good things, a direct fear-to-security-and-provision movement.

terra: The fixed measure of twelve months dates from Allah’s creation of heaven and earth, and the ayah calls this “the upright religion”; creation, temporal measure, and q-y-m religion meet directly.
terra: People are told to work; Allah, the Messenger, and believers will see the work, and everyone will be returned to the Knower who reports what they did.
terra: Every hardship and step borne in Allah's path is written as a righteous deed, because Allah does not waste the reward of good-doers.
terra: Every contribution and journey is recorded so Allah may reward the best of the people's work, extending 9:120's preserved accounting.
luna: The section's return from life's descent meets the promise that all return to God, إِلَيْهِ مَرْجِعُكُمْ جَمِيعًا; the verse ties that return to creation begun and repeated.
terra: Worldly life is rain-grown abundance whose owners think it secured, then Allah's command makes it reaped as though never flourishing, exposing provision's apparent durability.
terra: Every soul meets what it sent ahead, people are returned (رُدُّوا۟) to Allah their true Master, and their inventions vanish; the ayah joins assayed work, return, truth, and failed fabrication.
terra: The question asks whether any alleged partner begins creation and then repeats it; Allah alone does both, separating real creative power from invented partners.
terra: The Messenger is told to follow revelation and remain patient until Allah judges, “the best of judges,” turning the title into a stance of waiting under pressure.

luna: The section's word أَحْكَم joins securing workmanship against spoilage with judgment; this ayah uses the same root for a Book whose verses were made firm, أُحْكِمَتْ آيَاتُهُ. | terra: The Book’s ayat are “made firm” (أُحْكِمَتْ) and then detailed by the Wise One, displaying the nonjudicial sense of h-k-m as work secured against defect.
terra: Noah appeals to Allah’s true promise and calls Him “the wisest/best of judges” (أَحْكَمُ ٱلْحَٰكِمِينَ), the exact closing title placed in a concrete plea for judgment.
terra: Hūd asks no wage and says his wage rests only with the One who originated him, directly joining reward to real creation.

luna: The section's calibrated coin meets Shuʿayb's instruction to give full measure and weight justly, أَوْفُوا الْمِكْيَالَ وَالْمِيزَانَ بِالْقِسْطِ; the surrounding warning makes fraud consequential. | terra: Shuʿayb confronts a people whose practice concerns measure and weight; 11:85 supplies the positive command to make both full and just.

luna: The section's rejected underweight coin meets the repeated command to complete measure and weight and not diminish people's goods; the verse names the exact market wrong behind the image. | terra: The command to fulfill measure and weight with justice and not diminish goods gives the moneychanger image an ethical standard.
terra: The people made happy remain in the Garden and receive “a gift not cut off” (عَطَآءً غَيْرَ مَجْذُوذٍ), a direct synonym-scene for the uncut wage.
terra: Joseph's brothers ask why their father does not trust them with Joseph and claim sincere goodwill; 12:17 later exposes the scene's truth-and-trust problem.
terra: The brothers say their father will not believe them even if they are truthful, placing claimed truthfulness against the broken trust requested in 12:11.

terra: Joseph is sold for a few counted dirhams, a Quranic coin scene in which human beings themselves are drastically undervalued; the link is to the section’s dirham and assay image, not to a counterfeit coin.

luna: The section's uprightness and just judgment meet the statement that judgment belongs to God and this is the correct religion, الدِّينُ الْقَيِّمُ; it joins both senses of the section's root. | terra: “Judgment belongs only to Allah” and “that is the upright religion” (ٱلدِّينُ ٱلْقَيِّمُ) place the two semantic workshops of حكم and قوم together.
luna: The section's dictionary sense of أَمِين is dependable custody; Egypt's ruler calls Joseph trusted, أَمِينٌ, just as Joseph is appointed to guard provisions.
luna: The section's reliable beast and secure place meet Joseph asking to oversee the land's storehouses as a knowledgeable keeper; this neighbor explains the work attached to his trust.

terra: The brothers find “our merchandise returned to us” (بِضَٰعَتُنَا رُدَّتْ إِلَيْنَا); unlike the section’s defective dirham, this commercial return restores value and provision rather than rejecting it.
terra: Judah resolves to remain until his father permits him or Allah judges for him, and names Allah the best of judges; the formula governs a painful family impasse.
terra: When Joseph's shirt is placed on Jacob's face, he “returns seeing” (ٱرْتَدَّ بَصِيرًا), a restorative bodily reversal within the r-d-d family rather than decline.
terra: The question asks whether alleged partners created anything like Allah's creation so that the two creations seemed alike, then declares Allah the Creator of everything.
terra: Flood foam and smelting dross vanish as waste while what benefits people remains on earth, joining the moneyworker's furnace to the section's passing-versus-lasting assay.
terra: The promised garden has food and shade that are دائم, a concrete picture of provision that does not run out.
terra: The works of those who deny their Lord are like ashes violently scattered by wind, a specific scene of work retaining no weight or usable value.
terra: People exchange Allah's favor for disbelief and settle their people in the abode of ruin; 14:29 names Hell as that destination.
terra: Hell is the evil settlement reached after favor is exchanged for disbelief in 14:28, supplying the downward endpoint of the reversal.

luna: The section's safe town is repeated in Abraham's prayer for Mecca, رَبِّ اجْعَلْ هَٰذَا الْبَلَدَ آمِنًا; the prayer protects the place where he settles his family. | terra: Abraham asks Allah to make this land secure; 14:37 supplies the sacred valley and requested fruits, repeating the safe-city prayer.

luna: The section's safe place as ground for human life meets Abraham's settlement in a barren valley and prayer that hearts incline and fruits be provided; this neighbor completes the provision scene. | terra: Abraham places descendants by the Sacred House in an uncultivated valley and asks that they receive fruits, joining sacred location, barren ground, worship, and provision.
terra: Allah spreads earth, anchors it with mountains, and causes everything to grow in due measure, joining ground, fit proportion, and provision.
luna: The section's well-proportioned human meets God's announcement that He will create a human from sounding clay; this verse begins the explicit formation scene.

luna: The section's straightened body meets the completion of that creation when God has proportioned the human and breathed of His spirit, سَوَّيْتُهُ; this neighbor names the bodily act behind taqwim.
terra: No weariness touches the Garden's people and they are never expelled, reversing both the stranded traveler's exhaustion and an interrupted dwelling.
luna: The section's güvenli place meets people carving secure homes in mountains, آمِنِينَ; the next verse overturns their confidence.
luna: The section's descent from a safe town meets the sudden blast that seizes those who thought themselves secure; this neighbor supplies the reversal to 15:82.
terra: Allah creates the human from a drop, yet the human becomes an open adversary, another direct turn from real creation to the stance of denial.

luna: The section's reliable camel meets the Qur'anic account of livestock created for human benefit, including warmth and food; it supplies the practical setting for the carrying animals in the next verses.
luna: The section's sturdy animal and provision meet the beauty people find in bringing livestock home and taking them out to pasture; this neighbor continues the same animal scene.

luna: The section's dependable camel, exhausted traveler, and destination town converge in animals carrying heavy loads to a far country reachable only with great hardship, تَحْمِلُ أَثْقَالَكُمْ إِلَىٰ بَلَدٍ.
luna: The section's travel and load-bearing animal meet horses, mules, and donkeys provided for riding and adornment; this neighbor extends the journey scene beyond camels.
terra: Allah creates, causes death, and returns some people (يُرَدُّ) to the feeblest age until knowledge is lost, a direct repeated formulation of temporal return into bodily decline.
luna: The section's well-formed body meets human emergence from the mothers' wombs without knowledge, then hearing, sight, and hearts given by God; the verse makes bodily capacity a provision.

terra: “What is with you runs out, and what is with Allah remains,” followed by recompense for patient people according to their best deeds, states the section’s passing-versus-uncut-wage meeting almost as a definition.

luna: The section's secure, provision-bearing town has its reversal here: a secure, tranquil town rejects its blessing and is clothed with hunger and fear, لِبَاسَ الْجُوعِ وَالْخَوْفِ. | terra: The secure, tranquil town whose provision came abundantly then tastes hunger and fear after denying Allah’s favors is the section’s safe-provisioned city and its reversal in one scene.
terra: The believer who strives for the hereafter with its proper striving has that striving appreciated, an explicit statement that rightly directed labor retains value.

luna: The section's full-weight dinar and balanced judgment meet the instruction to fill the measure and weigh with the straight balance, الْقِسْطَاسِ الْمُسْتَقِيمِ. | terra: The command to give full measure and weigh with “the straight balance” (ٱلْقِسْطَاسِ ٱلْمُسْتَقِيمِ) is the Quranic counterpart of the full-standard coin and straight shaft.
terra: Allah honors Adam's children, carries and provides them, and gives them marked preference, the Quranic positive rank against the human being's possible lowering.
luna: The section's meeting of uprightness and crookedness in أَجْر is echoed by revelation with no عِوَج; this verse starts a passage that joins a straight book to lasting reward.

luna: The section's q-w-m root for uprightness meets the Qur'an called قَيِّمًا, then good news for believers who do righteous deeds and receive a good wage. | terra: The Book is قَيِّمًا and gives believers who do sound deeds “a good reward”; with the absence of crookedness in 18:1, this ayah directly joins straightness, righteous work, and recompense.
luna: The section's wage that does not end meets believers remaining in their reward forever, مَاكِثِينَ فِيهِ أَبَدًا; this completes the same passage's promise.
terra: Believers who do sound works are assured that Allah does not waste the reward of one who makes work good, directly stating successful workmanship and preserved wage.

luna: The section's bodily descent and lasting wage meet worldly life pictured as rain-grown plants that dry into windblown debris, هَشِيمًا تَذْرُوهُ الرِّيَاحُ; the next verse names what remains valuable. | terra: Worldly life is vegetation mixed with rain that becomes dry fragments scattered by wind, another concrete form of what cannot remain.

luna: The section's sound deeds and uncut reward meet the lasting righteous deeds, الْبَاقِيَاتُ الصَّالِحَاتُ, said to be better in reward and hope than transient wealth and children. | terra: Worldly wealth and children are adornment, while “the enduring righteous deeds” are better in reward and hope, concretely joining what remains, sound work, and recompense.
terra: Moses’s servant says their journey has brought them fatigue (نَصَبًا); it concretely stages the weary traveler used in the section to explain a life or reward being cut short.
terra: After the journey fatigue and lost fish of 18:62–63, Moses and his servant turn back on their tracks, joining the section's exhausted traveler image to literal reversal.

terra: The wall was about to fall, so the servant “set it upright” (فَأَقَامَهُ), and Moses immediately speaks of taking a wage (أَجْرًا); one ayah directly joins the section’s straightened workpiece to the worker’s pay.

terra: The uprighted wall conceals a treasure for two orphans whose father was righteous, and its repair is mercy rather than a bid for pay; this supplies the preserved value and sound deed behind the wage question in 18:77.
terra: Those who denied their Lord’s signs and meeting have null works, so no weight is established for them on Resurrection; rejected work and failed assay meet directly.
terra: The human asks whether he will be brought out alive after death; 19:67 answers denial of return with first creation.
terra: The human is reminded that Allah created him before when he was nothing, making first creation the answer to denied resurrection.
terra: “The enduring righteous deeds” are better in reward and “return” (مَرَدًّا), directly bringing lasting work, pay, and the r-d-d family into one line.

luna: The section's fire seen during Moses' journey is repeated as he notices a fire and hopes to bring a brand; this verse begins the neighboring call at 20:11–12. | terra: Moses perceives a fire and hopes to bring a brand or guidance from it; 20:11–12 reveal that the apparent fire has led him to the sacred valley and divine call.

luna: The section's fire scene continues when Moses reaches it and is called; the next verse identifies the sacred place, setting up the encounter's authority. | terra: When Moses reaches the fire he is called by name, the transition from the perceived object in 20:10 to the sacred valley in 20:12.

luna: The section's meeting at the Tur becomes an instruction at the sacred valley; this neighbor completes the scene's setting, though it does not itself name the later fear. | terra: The called Moses is told he is in the sacred valley of Ṭuwā, grounding the fire scene in the mountain-place invoked by surah 95.
luna: The section's Moses-at-the-Tur scene includes fear at a transformed form; this ayah shows the staff becoming a moving serpent, the startling event answered by reassurance in the next verse.

luna: The section's fear-to-safety meeting and return of a thing to its former state meet God's command to take the staff without fear and His promise to restore it, سَنُعِيدُهَا سِيرَتَهَا الْأُولَىٰ.

luna: The section's spatial and temporal dictionary senses of رَدَّ meet creation from earth, return into it, and emergence from it again, مِنْهَا نُخْرِجُكُمْ تَارَةً أُخْرَى. | terra: Humans are created from earth, returned into it, and brought out from it again, the complete bodily descent-and-rising movement in one ayah.
terra: Allah recalls deliverance, appoints the right side of the Mount, and sends down manna and quails as good provision, bringing the Mount, the m-n-n family, safety, and sustenance together.
terra: At the descent from the garden, Allah promises that whoever follows His guidance will neither go astray nor suffer, a guided boundary within the downward movement.
terra: Whoever turns from the reminder receives a constricted life and is raised blind, the opposite outcome to the protected followers in 20:123.
terra: The Prophet must not strain toward temporary worldly splendor; the Lord’s provision is better and more lasting, another explicit endurance boundary.

luna: The section's full-weight coin and just judgment meet scales set for Resurrection, الْمَوَازِينَ الْقِسْطَ; no soul is wronged even by a mustard seed. | terra: The just balances set for Resurrection weigh even a mustard seed and Allah suffices as reckoner, carrying the moneychanger’s exact assay into the divine court.
terra: For the believer who performs righteous works there is no rejection or ingratitude toward the effort, and it is written down, directly opposing the rejected-work image.

luna: The section explicitly links رَدَدْنَاهُ to life's return to its frailest age; this ayah names womb stages, that age, dead soil revived, and resurrection as evidence for the Hour. | terra: This ayah itself joins embryonic shaping, maturity, being returned (يُرَدُّ) to the feeblest age, and dead soil swelling into life, and frames all of them as evidence for resurrection doubters.
terra: After the life stages and revived field in 22:5, this ayah states their inference: Allah is the Truth, gives life to the dead, and is capable of everything.
terra: This ayah completes 22:5’s proof by naming the coming Hour and the raising of those in graves; it identifies what the revived field is meant to establish.

terra: The ayah pictures extending a cord toward heaven and then cutting it; it may recall the section’s lexical explanation of m-n-n through a severed rope, though the ayah’s difficult image serves a different argument about frustrated rage.

luna: The section's dictionary family for بَلَد includes a camel's side falling to earth; here sacrificial camels stand and then their sides fall, فَإِذَا وَجَبَتْ جُنُوبُهَا, before people eat and feed others.
luna: The section's outwardly measured deed and inwardly sound work meet the distinction that neither meat nor blood reaches God, but piety does; this neighbor explains what the sacrifice means.
terra: Allah removes Satan’s insertion and then “makes firm His signs” (يُحْكِمُ ٱللَّهُ ءَايَٰتِهِ), a Quranic enactment of protecting work from corruption.
terra: Those invoked besides Allah cannot create even a fly, and cannot recover what it takes from them, exposing both failed making and failed recovery.
luna: The section's dictionary form أَمِين names a dependable bearer; this verse values believers who keep trusts and covenants, وَالَّذِينَ هُمْ لِأَمَانَاتِهِمْ وَعَهْدِهِمْ رَاعُونَ.
luna: The section's human fashioned in best proportion meets the beginning of human creation from an extract of clay, سُلَالَةٍ مِّن طِينٍ.
luna: The section's upright body has a staged beginning; this next verse places the human drop in a secure resting place, قَرَارٍ مَّكِينٍ.

luna: The section's soundly fashioned body meets the stages ending in bones clothed with flesh and then a further creation; it gives bodily substance to its takwim image. | terra: The embryo passes through measured forms into bones clothed with flesh and another creation, displaying the workmanship later carried through death and rising in 23:15–16.

luna: The section's uncut reward meets the immediate reminder that humans die after their bodily formation; the verse marks the interruption that the next verse's resurrection answers. | terra: After the formed creation of 23:14, human beings die, the downward break before 23:16’s raising.

luna: The section's return and standing before judgment meet the promise that people will be raised on the Day of Resurrection; this neighbor completes the life-stage sequence. | terra: After death, people are raised on Resurrection Day, completing the formed-body, ending, and restored-standing sequence.
terra: A tree grows from Mount Sinai producing oil and food for eaters, directly joining the Mount, the olive, and provision that surah 95 distributes across its opening oaths.

luna: The section's root ر د د includes turning back; at death the wrongdoer asks to be sent back to do right, رَبِّ ارْجِعُونِ, linking return with unfinished work. | terra: At death the wrongdoer asks to be returned; 23:100 reveals that the desired return is to perform righteous work and that a barrier prevents it.

luna: The section's return and uncut-work meeting meets the barrier until resurrection; this neighbor explains why the requested return cannot supply a second chance before judgment. | terra: The dying person asks to return and do righteous work but is refused and held behind a barrier until resurrection, joining life's cut, return, and belated workmanship.

luna: The section's wages and the just balance meet those whose scales are heavy, الْمَوَازِينُ; this ayah makes the weight of a life's work decisive. | terra: Those whose scales are heavy are the successful, the positive side of the weighed judgment reversed in 23:103.

luna: The section's sound work and uncut reward meet the opposite case: light scales mean loss of self; the ayah gives the boundary to the promised outcome. | terra: Those whose scales are light lose themselves and remain in Hell, carrying deficient weight into the downward final outcome.

luna: The section's creation, return, and denial of dīn meet the question whether people thought they were created without purpose and would not be returned to God. | terra: The rhetorical question asks whether humans thought they were created aimlessly and would not be returned to Allah, directly fusing creation, return, and the surah's interrogative stance.
luna: The section's return to the just Judge meets the declaration that God is the true King and Lord of the noble Throne; this neighbor completes the answer to the claim of purposeless creation.
terra: Faithless works are a mirage that the thirsty person finds empty, only to find Allah there to settle the account in full; failed product and exact recompense meet.
terra: When people are called to Allah and His Messenger to judge between them, a group turns away, directly pairing adjudication with religious refusal.
terra: The believers' response when called for judgment is to hear and obey, the faithful counterpart to the turning away in 24:48.
terra: Allah promises believers who do righteous work succession, establishment of their religion, and replacement of fear with security, joining work, stable religion, and safety.
terra: Allah creates everything and determines it with exact determination, the broad Quranic formulation behind the section's made-fit and measured form.
terra: Allah turns to the deeds people performed and makes them scattered dust, the clearest scene of apparent work being rejected as worthless.

luna: The section's dictionary family for بَلَد joins a place to provision; this verse sends rain to revive a dead town and water people and livestock, without stating the resurrection comparison. | terra: Rain revives a dead land and gives drink to animals and many people, connecting dead soil, life, and distributed provision.
terra: Noah’s people “denied the messengers”; 26:107 calls Noah trustworthy and 26:109 places his wage with the Lord, giving the denial side of the section’s endurance-trust-wage triangle.
terra: Noah says, “I am to you a trustworthy messenger” (رَسُولٌ أَمِينٌ), between his people’s denial in 26:105 and his divine wage in 26:109.
terra: Noah asks no wage from the people and assigns his wage only to the Lord of the worlds, completing 26:105–107’s denial and trust scene.
terra: ʿĀd “denied the messengers”; 26:125 and 26:127 answer that denial with a trustworthy messenger whose wage is with Allah.
terra: Hūd’s claim to be a trustworthy messenger supplies the dependable side opposite ʿĀd’s denial in 26:123 and beside his wage statement in 26:127.
terra: Hūd asks no wage and places his wage with the Lord, completing the repeated denial-trust-unfailing-pay pattern.
terra: Thamūd “denied the messengers”; 26:143 and 26:145 supply the trustworthy messenger and his Lord-held wage.
terra: Ṣāliḥ says he is a trustworthy messenger, the stable claim set against denial in 26:141 and joined to divine wage in 26:145.
terra: Ṣāliḥ asks no wage and reserves his wage to the Lord, completing another exact recurrence of the section’s linked images.
terra: Lot’s people “denied the messengers”; 26:162 and 26:164 place a trustworthy messenger and his wage across from that denial.
terra: Lot declares himself a trustworthy messenger, directly opposing his people’s denial and preceding the statement of his wage.
terra: Lot asks no wage from his people and places his wage with the Lord, completing the trust-denial-wage refrain.
terra: The people of the thicket “denied the messengers”; 26:178 and 26:180 supply Shuʿayb’s trustworthiness and divine wage.
terra: Shuʿayb says he is a trustworthy messenger, the reliable side of the denial named in 26:176 and the wage named in 26:180.
terra: Shuʿayb asks no human wage and places his wage with the Lord, closing the surah’s repeated denial-trust-pay structure.

luna: The section's defective coin returned at the assayer's bench meets the command to complete the measure and not cause loss, أَوْفُوا الْكَيْلَ وَلَا تَكُونُوا مِنَ الْمُخْسِرِينَ. | terra: “Give full measure” and do not cause loss introduces the just commercial standard completed by the straight balance in 26:182.

luna: The section's coin must be properly calibrated; this continuation commands weighing with the even balance, وَزِنُوا بِالْقِسْطَاسِ الْمُسْتَقِيمِ. | terra: “Weigh with the straight balance” (ٱلْقِسْطَاسِ ٱلْمُسْتَقِيمِ) directly joins straightness and full assay.

luna: The section's rejected false coin corresponds to Shuʿayb's warning not to deprive people of their due or spread corruption; the verse supplies the ethical result of crooked measure. | terra: After full measure and a straight balance, the people are forbidden to diminish others’ things or spread corruption, explaining what faulty assay does socially.

luna: The section's Moses-and-fire scene recurs as Moses sees a fire and hopes to bring news or a burning brand; the next verses turn the scene to divine reassurance. | terra: Moses tells his family he perceives a fire and will bring news or a burning brand; 27:8–10 turn the sight into a divine meeting and reassurance from fear.

luna: The section's fire encounter is located in a blessed presence, with blessing on whoever is in or around it; this neighbor leads into the explicit reassurance at 27:9–10. | terra: At the fire Moses is called and told that the fire's surroundings are blessed; this gives the fire encounter its consecrated place before his fear in 27:10.
luna: The section's fire encounter turns fear toward safety; at this point in the same scene the voice identifies itself as God, grounding the following command not to fear.

luna: The section's fear-to-security movement at the Tur meets God's command not to fear in His presence; the staff scene turns fright into a protected encounter. | terra: Moses turns in flight from the moving staff and is told that messengers need not fear in Allah’s presence, repeating the fire encounter’s fear-to-safety turn.
terra: The Messenger is commanded to worship the Lord of “this town,” who made it sacred, joining place and submission as 30:30 joins creation and religion.

terra: The woman recommends hiring Moses because the best hire is “the strong, the trustworthy” (ٱلْقَوِىُّ ٱلْأَمِينُ), joining dependable strength to paid work just as the section joins emîn, the implement, and wage.
terra: The father offers Moses marriage in exchange for eight or ten years of labor, supplying the actual term and payment behind the trustworthy hire of 28:26.

luna: The section's Moses-at-the-Tur meeting begins when he sees a fire, آنَسَ مِن جَانِبِ الطُّورِ نَارًا; the following verse's encounter continues into fear and reassurance. | terra: Moses perceives a fire while traveling and turns toward it; 28:30–31 transform that distant fire scene into divine address and safety from fear.

luna: The section's fire scene becomes a divine call from the blessed side of the valley; this neighboring verse locates the encounter before 28:31 tells Moses not to fear. | terra: The call comes from the blessed side of the valley by the tree, locating the divine meeting between the fire of 28:29 and the reassurance of 28:31.

luna: The section connects Moses' fear at the fire to safety; God tells him not to fear and calls him among the secure, مِنَ الْآمِنِينَ, directly linking fear and trust. | terra: Moses turns away in fear when the staff moves and is told to return, approach, and be among the secure (ٱلْءَامِنِينَ), explicitly staging fear’s change into safety at the fire encounter.
terra: The objection that guidance would cost the Meccans their land is answered by the safe sanctuary to which fruits of every kind are gathered as provision.
terra: Many settlements exulting in their livelihood are destroyed and their dwellings left nearly uninhabited, a broad repeated scene of provisioned place reversed.
terra: Worldly goods are temporary enjoyment and adornment, while what is with Allah is better and more lasting, stating the two sides of depletion and endurance.
terra: Allah has praise in both lives, judgment is His, and “to Him you are returned”; judgment and return are again assigned to the same hand.

luna: The section's ending life, divine judgment, and return meet the statement that all things perish but God's face, الحكم belongs to Him, and people return to Him. | terra: Everything perishes except Allah’s face, while judgment belongs to Him and all are returned to Him; passing, remaining, return, and judgment meet in one ayah.

luna: The section distinguishes God's real creation from humanly fabricated falsehood; this ayah uses تَخْلُقُونَ إِفْكًا for the latter and turns directly to God as provider. | terra: The idolaters “fabricate a lie” (تَخْلُقُونَ إِفْكًا), while their fabricated gods cannot provide; this is the human false-making sense of kh-l-q set against Allah’s real creation and provision.
terra: “If you deny, communities before you denied” extends the fabrication scene of 29:17 and leads into the first-and-final creation proof of 29:19–20.
terra: People are asked whether they see how Allah begins creation and repeats it, the real making that answers the fabricated lie of 29:17.
terra: The command to travel and observe how creation began concludes that Allah will produce the final creation, turning first making into evidence for return.
luna: The section's life ending and return meet the statement that every soul tastes death and then returns to God; mortality does not cancel the final reckoning.
terra: Worldly life is diversion and play, while the hereafter is the true life, setting transient appearance against the life that does not fail.

luna: The section's safe town meets the protected sanctuary whose people remain secure while people around them are seized; the ayah makes the safety geographical and precarious. | terra: People see that Allah made a secure sanctuary while others are seized around it, yet they believe falsehood and reject His favor; safety and denial face each other directly.
terra: People are asked to reflect that Allah created in truth and for a fixed term, while many still deny meeting their Lord.

luna: The section's return after human creation meets the statement that God begins creation, repeats it, and to Him people return, ثُمَّ إِلَيْهِ تُرْجَعُونَ. | terra: Allah begins creation, repeats it, and then people are returned to Him, compressing making and return into one movement.
terra: Allah brings living from dead and dead from living, revives earth after its death, and says people will be brought out likewise.

luna: The section's best creation followed by return meets God's ability to originate creation and repeat it; this verse grounds the rise after descent in the Creator's power. | terra: Allah originates creation and repeats it, and the supreme attribute belongs to Him, a repeated creation-to-restoration formulation near 30:30's fitrah and upright religion.

luna: The section names this exact meeting: the command to set the face toward religion, the creation/fıṭra, and the root ق و م in الدِّينُ الْقَيِّمُ occur together here. | terra: The command to set the face upright for religion joins Allah’s human fitrah/creation, the unchangeable creation, and “the upright religion” (ٱلدِّينُ ٱلْقَيِّمُ), exactly gathering the section’s fourth meeting.
terra: Immediately after the fitrah and upright religion of 30:30, people are told to turn back to Allah, be mindful, establish prayer, and avoid association.
terra: The command to set the face toward “the upright religion” precedes a day that cannot be turned back from Allah, joining q-y-m religion to the boundary of return.
terra: The reader is told to look at how Allah revives earth after death; the same reviver will revive the dead, making the field a direct resurrection proof.
terra: Creation moves from weakness to strength and back to weakness and gray hair, making the rise-and-return arc of the human body explicit.
terra: After identifying the world as Allah's creation, the ayah challenges the audience to show what others created, drawing the boundary between real and claimed making.
terra: Whoever submits the face to Allah while doing good grasps the firmest handhold, joining directed religion, sound work, unbroken support, and return of all outcomes to Allah.

luna: The section's best-proportioned human meets God's making of all things good and the start of human creation from clay; the verse joins creation to fitness. | terra: Allah “made good everything He created” and began human creation from clay; 32:9–11 proceed through bodily fashioning, denial, death, and return.
luna: The section's human form meets the continuation from clay into progeny from a humble fluid; this neighbor specifies the bodily sequence.

luna: The section's upright, fitted person meets the verse saying He fashioned the human and breathed of His spirit into him; this is the closest creation-side counterpart. | terra: Allah fashioned the human, breathed spirit, and made hearing, sight, and hearts; the careful making is followed by ingratitude and resurrection denial in 32:10.
terra: People ask whether, once lost in earth, they can be in a new creation; this denial stands between divine formation in 32:9 and return in 32:11.
terra: The angel of death takes people and then they are returned to their Lord, answering 32:10’s denial and completing formation, descent into earth, and return.
terra: The guilty stand with heads lowered before their Lord and ask to be returned so they can do righteous work, directly combining descent, judgment, return, and failed labor.
terra: Believers are commanded to speak “a straight/right word” (قَوْلًا سَدِيدًا); 33:71 makes the consequence the repair of their deeds.
terra: Allah will “make sound for you your deeds” (يُصْلِحْ لَكُمْ أَعْمَٰلَكُمْ), giving the section’s explanation of ṣāliḥāt as unspoiled work an explicit verbal form.
terra: David is told to make full coats of armor, measure their links precisely, and do righteous work, a rare ayah where skilled manufacture, measure, and ṣāliḥ action coincide.
terra: Sheba receives two gardens and the invitation to eat the Lord’s provision in “a good land”; 34:16–17 show this provisioned place reversed by refusal and ingratitude.
terra: When Sheba turns away, the flood replaces its two productive gardens with bitter and sparse growth, staging provision’s withdrawal from a favored place.
terra: The reversal is explicitly called recompense for ingratitude, making the ruined provision an assayed outcome rather than an arbitrary fall.
terra: Settlements on the journey are made visible and travel in them is secure by night and day; 34:19 shows this durable safety undone by the people’s demand.
terra: The people ask that their journeys be lengthened, wrong themselves, and are scattered, reversing the secure measured road of 34:18.
terra: Believers who do righteous works receive multiplied recompense and dwell secure in elevated chambers, combining sound work, wage, height, and security.

luna: The section's land/place image meets a dead town revived by rain, بَلَدٍ مَّيِّتٍ, followed by the explicit comparison to resurrection, كَذَٰلِكَ النُّشُورُ. | terra: Winds and clouds revive a dead land, and the ayah concludes “such is the resurrection,” repeating 22:5’s field-to-rising inference.
terra: Good speech rises and righteous work lifts it or is raised with it, while evil plotting perishes; upright ascent, sound work, and failed work are set together.
terra: Creation from dust and a drop is joined to every lengthening or shortening of lifespan being recorded, directly combining human making with measured age.

luna: The section's reward beyond life's end meets the people of Paradise praising God for removing sorrow; this neighbor leads to the next verse's explicit statement that fatigue no longer touches them.

luna: The section's unexhausted wage meets the secure home where no weariness touches its people; this neighboring verse completes the contrast with the traveler's exhaustion. | terra: The people of the lasting abode say neither weariness nor fatigue touches them, answering the section’s dictionary picture of the exhausted traveler stranded on the way.
terra: Whoever is granted long life is “reversed in creation” (نُنَكِّسْهُ فِى ٱلْخَلْقِ), stating without r-d-d the same bodily turn from upright strength toward decline.
terra: The human created from a drop becomes an open adversary, directly turning real creation into the stance that disputes resurrection.

luna: The section's dictionary form for أَجْر includes a bone set crooked; this ayah raises the challenge of reviving decayed bones and thus makes the lexical bone image literal. | terra: The denier forgets his own creation and asks who can revive decayed bones, staging the broken body that divine making must restore.

luna: The section's straightening and creation meeting is answered by the One who made bones the first time; this neighboring verse grounds restoration in original creation. | terra: The answer is that the One who originated the bones the first time will revive them, opposing remembered real creation to the denier’s claim.
luna: The section contrasts God's true creation with human fabrication; Abraham asks about worshipping what people carve, مَا تَنْحِتُونَ, making human craft the scene's concrete example.
luna: The section says the root خ ل ق separates God's creation from human making; this neighboring ayah says God created both people and what they do, وَاللَّهُ خَلَقَكُمْ وَمَا تَعْمَلُونَ.
terra: The disbelieving leaders dismiss the message as “a fabrication” (ٱخْتِلَٰقٌ), a direct Quranic use of the kh-l-q family for invented making rather than Allah's real creation.
terra: Paradise provision is declared to have “no depletion” (مَا لَهُۥ مِن نَّفَادٍ), making perceptible the same refusal of exhaustion as غَيْرُ مَمْنُونٍ.
luna: The section's best-formed human meets the repeated announcement of a human created from clay; this is a second Qur'anic telling of the formation scene.
luna: The section's fashioned body meets the continuation in which God proportions the human and breathes of His spirit; this neighboring retelling confirms the same creation-to-form sequence.
terra: Allah asks Iblis why he refused to bow to the human created by His hands and whether he claims to be among the exalted, placing true creation against false self-height.
terra: Iblis is expelled and accursed after claiming superiority over the created human, completing 38:75's reversal from imagined height to descent.
luna: The section's formed human and return through bodily stages meet creation in the womb, خَلْقًا مِّن بَعْدِ خَلْقٍ; this ayah adds the hidden stages before birth.
terra: Those who do good receive good, Allah's earth is spacious, and the patient are paid their reward without reckoning, setting divine wage beyond ordinary measure.
terra: Water produces varied crops that then wither, yellow, and become debris, making earthly provision's measured rise and exhaustion visible.
terra: Allah takes souls at death and during sleep, retains the one decreed to die, and releases the other until a fixed term, making life's ending and measured continuation explicit.
terra: The warning that association would nullify the addressee’s work sets a hard boundary around which work retains value.
terra: After the second trumpet blast, the dead are suddenly standing and looking, a direct repeated scene of human beings standing for final judgment.
terra: The present life is only temporary enjoyment, while the hereafter is the lasting abode, another explicit statement of what passes and what remains.

luna: The section's أَحْسَنِ تَقْوِيم is matched by God shaping people and making their forms good, صَوَّرَكُمْ فَأَحْسَنَ صُوَرَكُمْ; provision and lordship complete the setting. | terra: Allah makes earth a settlement and heaven a structure, forms people and makes their forms good, then provides good things; workmanship, place, and provision meet directly.

luna: The section's return to the weakest age meets the sequence from dust and a drop through maturity and old age; the verse makes death before the appointed term part of that same measure. | terra: The ayah counts creation from dust and drop through maturity and old age, with some taken earlier, another full Quranic enumeration of the life scale developed in 22:5.

luna: The section's أَجْر غَيْرُ مَمْنُونٍ is repeated for believers who do good, لَهُمْ أَجْرٌ غَيْرُ مَمْنُونٍ; the same wording makes reward's unbroken duration explicit. | terra: Belief and righteous deeds receive “a reward never cut off” (أَجْرٌ غَيْرُ مَمْنُونٍ), the exact formula whose lexical images the section unfolds.
terra: Allah sets firm mountains, blesses earth, and measures its sustenance, explicitly uniting stable construction, measure, place, and provision.
luna: The section's straight stature and lasting reward meet those who say God is their Lord and then remain steadfast, اسْتَقَامُوا; the angels promise them the Garden.
terra: The humbled earth stirs and swells when water descends; its reviver is declared able to revive the dead, a close nonlexical repeat of 22:5.
terra: Whatever people differ about has its judgment with Allah, to whom the speaker turns and upon whom he relies, joining adjudication and directed return.
terra: Allah sends the Book with truth and the balance, and the same ayah warns that the Hour may be near; revealed standard, assay, and judgment meet directly.
terra: Worldly provision is temporary enjoyment, while what is with Allah is better and more lasting for believers who trust their Lord, joining permanence to faith and reliance.

luna: The section's town and ground meeting includes land that can collapse or revive; this ayah calls rain to a dead town and compares it with people being raised. | terra: Measured water revives a dead land, followed by “thus will you be brought out,” joining measure, provision, earth, and resurrection.
terra: Allah creates heaven and earth in truth so every soul may be repaid for what it earned without injustice, joining real creation to exact wage.
luna: The section's return and judgment oppose those who claim only worldly life and deny that anything destroys them but time; this ayah gives the exact denial the image answers.
luna: The section's life, death, and return meet God's statement that He gives life and causes death and will gather people for the Day of Resurrection.
terra: Every community is seen kneeling and called to its record to be repaid for its works, combining bodily posture, inspected work, and judgment.
terra: Allah's record speaks truth because every work was copied, supplying the reliable account behind the verdict in 45:28.
terra: Heaven and earth are created in truth for a fixed term, yet the disbelievers turn away from the warning, placing measured creation against denial.
luna: The section's uprightness that holds through time meets those who affirm God as Lord and remain steadfast; the verse promises them freedom from fear and grief.
luna: The section's fatigued traveler and return from bodily decline meet the question whether the Creator, who made heaven and earth without weariness, can revive the dead.
terra: Paradise contains rivers of milk whose taste never changes; this stable milk reverses the section’s dictionary image of kezebe, milk that fails before its expected term.
terra: Believers are called “the uppermost,” and Allah promises He will not diminish their deeds; height and work whose value is not cut down meet in the same promise.
terra: Allah confirms that the believers will enter the Sacred Mosque secure and without fear, a direct repeated sacred-place and safety scene.
terra: People count their Islam as a favor (يَمُنُّونَ), but Allah says the true favor is His guidance to faith; this distinct m-n-n sense tests who can claim credit for belief and reward.
terra: Blessed rain produces gardens and harvest grain; 50:11 identifies this food as provision and likens the revived land to emergence from death.
terra: Tall palms with layered fruit clusters supply the provisioned growth between blessed rain in 50:9 and resurrection analogy in 50:11.

luna: The section's town, soil, and provision converge in this ayah: a dead land is revived as provision for servants, and the resurrection is likened to that emergence. | terra: Rain-provision revives a dead land and is followed by “thus is the emergence,” making food from earth a figure of human rising.

luna: The section's exhausted traveler and mortal life meet the denial that the Creator was wearied by the first creation; the verse contrasts human fatigue with God's power to create anew. | terra: Allah asks whether first creation wearied Him and identifies the deniers’ confusion about a new creation, directly placing making and doubt face to face.
terra: The oath “By the Mount” repeats the sworn object of surah 95 and anchors the Moses-place meeting in another divine oath.
terra: A human being has only what he strives for; 53:40–41 then show the work inspected and paid in full, like a craft presented for assay.
terra: The striving “will be seen,” supplying the inspection between labor in 53:39 and full recompense in 53:41.
terra: The inspected striving is repaid with “the fullest recompense,” completing the work-and-full-weight wage scene.
terra: Allah creates the male and female pair; 53:46 names their drop and 53:47 makes the second bringing-forth His responsibility.
terra: The created pair comes from an emitted drop, supplying the material stage between creation in 53:45 and renewed creation in 53:47.
terra: The second bringing-forth belongs to Allah, completing the first-creation and return sequence of 53:45–46.
terra: “Everything We created according to measure” states the relation between creation and exact proportion in its most compressed form.

luna: The section's full-weight dinar and just judgment meet the placed balance, الْمِيزَانُ; this verse introduces the measure whose justice the next ayat specify. | terra: Allah raises the heaven and sets the balance, joining height to measured order immediately before the command to establish weight in 55:9.

luna: The section's coin that fails its standard meets the command not to transgress the balance, الْمِيزَانِ; the measure is a moral boundary as well as a physical one. | terra: The prohibition on transgressing the balance states the failure that 55:9's established just weight prevents.

luna: The section's calibrated dinar and just verdict meet the command to establish weight in justice, الْوَزْنَ بِالْقِسْطِ; the ayah joins accurate measure to fairness. | terra: “Establish the weight with justice” (أَقِيمُوا۟ ٱلْوَزْنَ بِٱلْقِسْطِ) directly joins q-w-m uprightness to an undiminished scale.
terra: The coming Event is “lowering, raising,” assigning both vertical reversals to the one judgment the section says lowers and decides.
terra: Garden fruit is “neither cut off nor forbidden,” a concrete paradisal opposite to the section’s rope, lifespan, milk, and traveler images of interruption.
terra: “We created you; why do you not affirm?” turns human creation into the same pointed question that surah 95 directs at denial.
terra: Allah decrees death among people and cannot be outstripped, beginning the return side of the creation argument in 56:57–62.
terra: Allah can replace people with their likes and create them in a form they do not know, linking bodily form to divine power over return.
terra: Knowledge of the first creation is made the reason to remember and accept the next, completing 56:57’s creation question.
terra: Worldly life is vegetation that pleases, then yellows and becomes debris, while the afterlife holds punishment or enduring forgiveness, a full passing-versus-remaining comparison.
terra: Scripture and the balance are sent so people may “stand for justice,” and iron has mighty force; q-w-m, equitable measure, judgment, and the crafted metal implement meet here.
terra: Believing migrant women are not to be returned to the disbelievers, and the rule is immediately called Allah’s judgment between the parties, joining nonreturn and الحكم in one legal scene.
terra: Allah loves those who strive in a row like a solidly joined structure, a nonlexical picture of bodies and workmanship made firm against collapse.
terra: At death a person asks for a short delay in order to give and become righteous, making the ending lifespan the point at which further sound work is cut off.
terra: Allah will not delay a soul once its term arrives, closing the request in 63:10 and fixing the boundary between mortal work and its later wage.

luna: The section's best form meets the statement that God created and shaped people well, وَصَوَّرَكُمْ فَأَحْسَنَ صُوَرَكُمْ; this verse also points toward the return. | terra: Allah created in truth, formed people, and made their forms good, then names the final destination to Him; fine formation and return share the ayah.
terra: Whoever trusts Allah finds Him sufficient; Allah brings His purpose to completion and has set a measure for everything, joining reliance, durability, completion, and measure.

luna: The section's work judged for an uncut wage meets the reason God created death and life: to test who is best in deed, أَحْسَنُ عَمَلًا. | terra: Allah creates death and life to test who is best in deed, joining created mortality to the quality-assay of human work.
terra: Allah’s layered creation contains no inconsistency, and the viewer is told to return the gaze to seek a crack, like a finished work subjected to inspection for defect.
terra: The gaze is returned twice and comes back humbled and weary, unable to find the defect; repeated return confirms the Maker’s flawless work.
terra: Allah makes earth manageable, commands people to walk its paths and eat His provision, and ends with resurrection to Him; place, livelihood, and rising meet.
terra: The secure person is asked whether he feels safe from the earth swallowing him, making bodily descent the boundary of presumed security.
terra: The next question asks whether one feels safe from a storm sent from heaven, completing the warning that worldly security can be withdrawn.

luna: The section's dictionary root م ن ن links the wage that is not cut off; this ayah promises the Prophet a reward that is غير ممنون, using the same phrase. | terra: Allah directly promises the addressed Messenger “a reward never cut off,” preserving the exact phrase while changing the addressee from the faithful group to the Prophet.
luna: The section's root أ م ن joins security and dependability; this repeated Qur'anic description praises those who guard trusts and covenants, here among the traits of the praying steadfast.
terra: Allah caused human beings to grow from the earth like growth; 71:18 supplies their return into it and renewed emergence.
terra: Allah returns people into earth and brings them out anew, explicitly turning burial ground into the route of restored creation.

terra: The command not to give or confer favor seeking increase uses the m-n-n family in an action-and-return setting, a different sense from “uncut” reward that guards work from self-interested accounting.

luna: The section's dictionary family for أَجْر includes a bone that heals crookedly; this verse asks whether human bones will be gathered after death, making the bone image bodily and eschatological. | terra: The human doubts that Allah will gather his bones; 75:4 answers with the even finer precision of restoring fingertips.

luna: The section's bone-straightening sense meets God's ability to proportion even fingertips, بَنَانَهُ; the verse shows precise restoration rather than a crooked repair. | terra: Allah is able to proportion even the fingertips, carrying the section’s exact bodily workmanship through death and reassembly.

luna: The section asks what can still make a person deny the Recompense after creation and return; this ayah asks whether a human thinks he will be left without purpose, أَيَحْسَبُ الْإِنسَانُ أَن يُتْرَكَ سُدًى.
luna: The section's crafted human form meets the origin as a drop of emitted fluid; this verse begins the same creation-to-resurrection argument.

luna: The section's proportioned body meets the formation of a clot into a fashioned human, فَخَلَقَ فَسَوَّى; the verse gives the process behind the image. | terra: From a clot Allah “created and proportioned” the human, the same creation-and-straightening pair, before 75:40 asks about reviving the dead.
luna: The section's completed human form meets the creation of the two sexes from that fashioned beginning; the verse extends the body's measured making.

luna: The section's created human who may fall is asked whether the Creator can revive the dead; this neighbor turns formation directly toward return. | terra: The rhetorical question asks whether the One who fashioned the sexes is not able to revive the dead, matching surah 95’s closing argumentative stance.
terra: Allah creates the human from a mixed drop as a test and equips him with hearing and sight; 76:3 gives the divergent faithful and ungrateful responses.
terra: Allah guides the human to the way, whether grateful or ungrateful, setting two responses before the carefully formed creature of 76:2.
terra: The question recalls creation from a lowly fluid; 77:22–23 place it for a measured term and 77:24 confronts deniers.
terra: “We determined, and excellent are We at determining” makes exact measure the divine work immediately before the warning to deniers.
terra: “Woe that day to the deniers” follows the created and measured embryo, another compressed meeting of formation and takdhîb.
terra: The earth is made a gathering container, and 77:26 specifies that it holds both living and dead bodies.
terra: The earth contains “living and dead,” giving the section’s place-family image its graveward bodily face.
terra: The Spirit and angels stand in ranks on the Day when none speaks without permission, another concrete courtly standing before the Lord.

luna: The section's human made in best proportion meets the question of what material he was created from; the following verses trace the making that precedes death and reawakening. | terra: The question “From what did He create him?” begins a compact life sequence that reaches measured formation, death, burial, and resurrection.

luna: The section's measured human formation meets creation from a drop and its apportionment, فَقَدَّرَهُ; this verse names the fitting of human life. | terra: Allah creates the human from a drop and measures him, joining material creation to deliberate proportion.
luna: The section's course from upright creation toward descent meets the way made easy for human life; the next verses continue through death and reawakening.

luna: The section's descent and the life that ends meet the statement that God causes the human to die and be buried, فَأَقْبَرَهُ. | terra: Allah causes the human to die and places him in a grave, the groundward stage between measured creation and raising.

luna: The section's return and standing meet the promise that when God wills He will raise the buried human, أَنْشَرَهُ; this completes the neighboring death sequence. | terra: When Allah wills, He raises the buried human, completing the creation-to-ground-to-standing movement.

luna: The section's human made in best proportion meets the question of who created, proportioned, and balanced the person, خَلَقَكَ فَسَوَّاكَ فَعَدَلَكَ; this starts the form-to-religion sequence. | terra: The Creator “created you, fashioned you, and balanced you”; 82:9 then turns from that careful making to denial of the Judgment, reproducing the section’s creation-to-dîn sequence.

luna: The section's human form meets God's composition into whatever form He willed, فِي أَيِّ صُورَةٍ مَّا شَاءَ رَكَّبَكَ; the verse completes the bodily sequence before denial of judgment. | terra: Allah composes the human being in whatever form He wills; between the balancing of 82:7 and denial in 82:9, this ayah supplies the particular bodily form made by the craftsman.

luna: The section places creation and form before denial of dīn; this ayah says people deny the Recompense, بِالدِّينِ, immediately after 82:7–8's forming. | terra: “Yet you deny the Judgment” (تُكَذِّبُونَ بِٱلدِّينِ) follows the making and balancing of 82:7–8, exactly placing takdhîb against divine formation.

luna: The section's counterfeit, returned by the assayer, meets the woe pronounced on those who give short measure, الْمُطَفِّفِينَ; this is the closest direct image of defective weighing. | terra: The woe to fraudulent measurers opens the commercial assay scene that ends with people standing before the Lord in 83:6.

luna: The section's weighing bench meets the act of taking a full measure for oneself, اكْتَالُوا عَلَى النَّاسِ; this verse begins the imbalance the following verse reverses. | terra: The fraudsters demand full measure when receiving from others, supplying the self-serving standard behind the section’s sound and faulty money.

luna: The section's true-weight coin opposes giving others less when measuring or weighing, يُخْسِرُونَ; the ayah exposes the same standard applied differently to self and neighbor. | terra: When measuring or weighing for others they cause loss, the direct opposite of a full-weight dinar and just judgment.

luna: The section's measure-and-verdict meeting continues into the question whether the short-measurers expect to be raised; this verse contributes the link between market deceit and the afterlife reckoning. | terra: The question whether the defrauders expect to be raised turns the market scale of 83:2–3 toward the final standing of 83:6.

luna: The section's wage and judgment scenes converge in the great day named here, يَوْمٍ عَظِيمٍ; this ayah completes the question begun at 83:4 before people stand. | terra: The defrauders are raised “for a tremendous day,” identifying the judicial time between the resurrection question in 83:4 and the standing in 83:6.

luna: The section explicitly brings in the root ق و م through the standing of people before the Judge; this ayah says يَوْمَ يَقُومُ النَّاسُ لِرَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ. | terra: Human beings stand (يَقُومُ ٱلنَّاسُ) before the Lord of all worlds after the surrounding weighing fraud and resurrection question, completing the section’s movement from assay to standing before the Judge.

luna: The section's exhausted traveler and life's labor meet the address to humanity: you toil toward your Lord and will meet Him, كَادِحٌ إِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ كَدْحًا. | terra: The human being labors toward the Lord and will meet Him, placing every worker and work on a path to the final encounter whose enduring wage appears in 84:25.

luna: The section's phrase أَجْرٌ غَيْرُ مَمْنُونٍ recurs for believers who do righteous deeds; its placement after the deniers' fate sharpens the lasting reward's contrast. | terra: Belief and righteous deeds receive “a reward never cut off,” exactly repeating the sixth ayah’s work-and-enduring-wage formula.
terra: The human is commanded to consider what he was created from, opening a creation argument whose conclusion in 86:8 is Allah’s power to return him.
terra: After naming the fluid from which the person was made, the ayah says Allah is able “to return him” (رَجْعِهِ), directly linking creation to return.
terra: Allah “created and proportioned” (خَلَقَ فَسَوَّىٰ), the direct parallel to the made and straightened human form; 87:3 adds measure and guidance.
terra: Allah “measured and guided” (قَدَّرَ فَهَدَىٰ), showing that the well-made form also has an assigned measure and direction, completing 87:2’s creation.

luna: The section's wage that outlasts bodily life meets people preferring the nearer life, الْحَيَاةَ الدُّنْيَا; this verse names the choice opposed by enduring reward. | terra: People prefer the nearer life; 87:17 answers that preference with the better and more lasting afterlife, the section’s short-lived versus enduring line.

luna: The section's uncut wage meets the declaration that the Hereafter is better and more enduring, وَالْآخِرَةُ خَيْرٌ وَأَبْقَىٰ; it states why the nearer life is not final. | terra: The afterlife is “better and more lasting,” directly naming the enduring side opposite the preferred nearer life of 87:16.
terra: Faces are “working, exhausted” (عَامِلَةٌ نَّاصِبَةٌ) yet enter fire in 88:4, the hard opposite of sound work receiving an uncut wage.
terra: The exhausted workers of 88:3 enter a blazing fire, completing the reversal of labor whose outcome is punishment rather than enduring wage.
terra: Other faces are pleased with their striving, the successful counterpart to the exhausted but rejected labor of 88:3.
luna: The section's dictionary sense of أَمُون is a dependable camel; this ayah directly invites readers to look at camels, الْإِبِلِ, and how they were created.
luna: The section brings a well-formed human into a meeting with height and place; after the camel, this neighboring ayah asks readers to consider how heaven was raised.
luna: The section's straight, measured forms meet the next object in the same contemplation: mountains set firmly in place; this ayah continues the camel-and-creation scene.
luna: The section's safe town and earth-bound descent meet the final object in the contemplation, the earth spread out; this verse completes the sequence begun with the camel.

luna: The section's oath by the secure town meets another oath by this town, هَٰذَا الْبَلَدِ; the next verses move from place and family to human creation. | terra: An oath by “this city” begins a surah that says in 90:4 “We created the human,” a striking structural parallel to surah 95’s city oath and human creation.
luna: The section's place as a setting for human life meets the address to the Prophet in this town; this neighbor continues the oath before parent and child.
luna: The section places the town oath beside human formation; this neighbor adds parent and child, وَوَالِدٍ وَمَا وَلَدَ, before the claim about human toil.

luna: The section's bodily formation and exhausted traveler meet the statement that humanity was created in hardship, فِي كَبَدٍ; the town oath and human condition meet in one surah. | terra: “We created the human in toil” supplies the human condition after the city oath of 90:1, parallel to surah 95 while replacing best proportion with struggle.
terra: Feeding on a day of hunger gives concrete righteous work inside the city-oath surah, countering the hunger that clothes the ungrateful town of 16:112.
terra: Feeding a poor person “in dust” places the low, earth-clinging body within the upward moral path of the city-oath surah.
terra: After freeing and feeding, the climbers of the steep path are those who believe and counsel patience and mercy, another belief-and-work exception after human toil.

luna: The section's fitting and straightening image meets the proportioned soul, سَوَّاهَا; this ayah makes formation the premise for the moral alternatives in the next verses. | terra: The oath turns to the soul and the One who proportioned it, another direct image of human inner form made fit.

luna: The section's sound work versus crookedness meets the soul made to recognize its wickedness and piety; this neighbor names the moral measure of what follows. | terra: The fashioned soul is shown its corruption and mindfulness, identifying the moral alternatives within the proportioned creation of 91:7.

luna: The section's صالحات and enduring wage meet success through purifying the soul, قَدْ أَفْلَحَ مَن زَكَّاهَا; this is the positive course after formation. | terra: The one who purifies the fashioned soul succeeds, the soundly maintained side of the form described in 91:7.

luna: The section's fall to the lowest is illuminated by the soul's failure when buried in corruption, وَقَدْ خَابَ مَن دَسَّاهَا; the neighbor states formation's contrary outcome. | terra: The one who corrupts or buries the fashioned soul fails, the moral deformation opposite purification in 91:9.
terra: Allah creates the human from a clinging form; 96:8 later identifies the return to the same Lord, giving another compact creation-and-return span.
terra: “To your Lord is the return” closes the challenge to the self-sufficient human who was reminded of creation in 96:2.
terra: Sincere worship, prayer, and alms are named as “the religion of uprightness” (دِينُ ٱلْقَيِّمَةِ); 98:7–8 then connect righteous work to created rank and lasting reward.
terra: Faithless deniers are called the worst of creatures, the low side of the rank whose opposite appears with righteous workers in 98:7.
terra: Believers who do righteous deeds are called the best of creatures, joining work to the restored human rank opposite 98:6.
terra: The best creatures receive their reward and abiding gardens, completing 98:5–7’s upright religion, sound work, rank, and enduring recompense.
luna: The section's dictionary family for بَلَد includes ground and buried bodies; this ayah begins with the earth shaken at the Resurrection, when the hidden dead are about to emerge.
luna: The section's ground, grave, and bodily descent meet the earth casting out its burdens, أَثْقَالَهَا; this neighbor makes the buried bodies part of the reckoning scene.

luna: The section's return before judgment meets people emerging in separate groups to be shown their deeds; the ayah links the earth's release to individual accounting. | terra: People emerge separately to be shown their deeds, supplying the resurrection-and-inspection scene completed by the atom-weight outcomes in 99:7–8.

luna: The section's calibrated worth and lasting wage meet even an atom's weight of good being seen, مِثْقَالَ ذَرَّةٍ خَيْرًا; no deed is too small to count. | terra: Whoever does an atom’s weight of good sees it, joining minute weight to the visibility and recompense of work.

luna: The section's sound work and reward meet the matching atom's weight of evil being seen; this neighbor completes the balanced accounting of 99:7. | terra: Whoever does an atom’s weight of evil sees it, giving the divine scale its opposite pan and its judgment boundary.

luna: The section's fitting deed and full-value wage meet the heavy scales, ثَقُلَتْ مَوَازِينُهُ; the image of measured value becomes the criterion for a good life. | terra: The one whose scales are heavy enters a pleasing life, beginning a direct weighed-outcome contrast completed by 101:8–9.
luna: The section's lasting wage meets the pleasing life that follows heavy scales; this verse names what the successful measure yields.

luna: The section's sound work meets the explicit opposite of a light balance, خَفَّتْ مَوَازِينُهُ; this verse starts the contrary fate to the enduring wage. | terra: The one whose scales are light receives the opposite verdict to 101:6, making deficient weight itself the turning point.

luna: The section's descent and its mention of Hell's lowest level meet the abyss, هَاوِيَةٌ, assigned to the light-scaled; this verse completes that reversal. | terra: The light-scaled person’s refuge is the abyss, joining failed weight to literal downward destination.

luna: The section's expiring life and wages that do not expire meet humanity being in loss, إِنَّ الْإِنسَانَ لَفِي خُسْرٍ; the next ayah names the exception. | terra: Humanity is declared in loss, the general downward condition from which 103:3 exempts believers and righteous workers just as 95:6 does.

luna: The section's believers, sound deeds, and exclusion from descent meet those exempted from loss by faith, righteous work, truth, and patience. | terra: The exception for those who believe, do righteous works, and uphold truth and patience closely parallels the exception from human descent in 95:6.

luna: The section's secure sanctuary meets the command to worship the Lord of this House; the next verse explains the concrete gifts attached to that place. | terra: The command to worship “the Lord of this House” fixes the source of the feeding and security named in 106:4.

luna: The section's safe town joins security with sustenance; God feeds its people against hunger and secures them from fear, أَطْعَمَهُم مِّن جُوعٍ وَآمَنَهُم مِّنْ خَوْفٍ. | terra: Allah feeds Quraysh against hunger and secures them against fear, the concise positive counterpart to the reversed town in 16:112.
